title: The wall of fog
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover is the fog offshore: a wall, white, the bay in sun before it, the town's shadow. The owner says it's a blank page. Wood says it's fog. She says he could have drawn something in it. He says he did. The strip lets her look.

panels.composition: The cover: a wall of fog across the top two-thirds, white, the bay in sun below, the seawall's shadow. Almost nothing.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover that is mostly white fog with a strip of sunlit bay and a seawall's shadow at the bottom, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner holding it. WOOD. BARNABY.

balloons.text: You could've drawn something in it.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a nearly blank booklet cover up and looking at it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner looking. The fog. In it, faint, a gull, two strokes, white on white.

image.prompt: close on a mostly white booklet cover with a faint two-stroke bird shape barely visible in the fog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner setting it in the rack. Nothing said. The strip lets her look and that's enough.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner placing a nearly blank booklet in a wire rack in silence, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The gull in the fog, white on white. She finds it.
